name: ros2-python-pkg
description: ROS 2 (rclpy) Python package: a node publishing heartbeat + /cmd_vel with a launch file. Build with colcon.

files.content:
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<?xml-model href="http://download.ros.org/schema/package_format3.xsd" schematypens="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"?>
<package format="3">
  <name>my_robot</name>
  <version>0.0.1</version>
  <description>Grg Code ROS 2 starter node.</description>
  <maintainer email="you@example.com">you</maintainer>
  <license>MIT</license>

  <exec_depend>rclpy</exec_depend>
  <exec_depend>std_msgs</exec_depend>
  <exec_depend>geometry_msgs</exec_depend>

  <test_depend>ament_copyright</test_depend>
  <test_depend>ament_flake8</test_depend>
  <test_depend>ament_pep257</test_depend>

  <export>
    <build_type>ament_python</build_type>
  </export>
</package>

from setuptools import setup
import os
from glob import glob

package_name = "my_robot"

setup(
    name=package_name,
    version="0.0.1",
    packages=[package_name],
    data_files=[
        ("share/ament_index/resource_index/packages", ["resource/" + package_name]),
        ("share/" + package_name, ["package.xml"]),
        (os.path.join("share", package_name, "launch"), glob("launch/*.launch.py")),
    ],
    install_requires=["setuptools"],
    zip_safe=True,
    maintainer="you",
    maintainer_email="you@example.com",
    description="Grg Code ROS 2 starter node (heartbeat + cmd_vel).",
    license="MIT",
    entry_points={
        "console_scripts": [
            "robot_node = my_robot.robot_node:main",
        ],
    },
)

import rclpy
from rclpy.node import Node
from geometry_msgs.msg import Twist
from std_msgs.msg import String


class RobotNode(Node):
    """Publishes a heartbeat and a demo /cmd_vel; subscribes to /cmd_vel to log it."""

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__("robot_node")
        self.declare_parameter("rate", 2.0)
        rate = self.get_parameter("rate").value
        self.hb = self.create_publisher(String, "heartbeat", 10)
        self.cmd = self.create_publisher(Twist, "cmd_vel", 10)
        self.create_subscription(Twist, "cmd_vel", self.on_cmd, 10)
        self.create_timer(1.0 / rate, self.tick)
        self.get_logger().info("robot_node up at %.1f Hz" % rate)

    def tick(self):
        m = String(); m.data = "alive"; self.hb.publish(m)
        t = Twist(); t.linear.x = 0.1; t.angular.z = 0.0; self.cmd.publish(t)

    def on_cmd(self, msg: Twist):
        self.get_logger().info("cmd_vel v=%.2f w=%.2f" % (msg.linear.x, msg.angular.z))


def main(args=None):
    rclpy.init(args=args)
    node = RobotNode()
    try:
        rclpy.spin(node)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
    finally:
        node.destroy_node()
        rclpy.shutdown()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# my_robot - ROS 2 Python package

A minimal ament_python package: a node that publishes a heartbeat + a demo `/cmd_vel` and logs `/cmd_vel`. See the `ros2` skill.

## Build & run (ROS 2 Humble/Jazzy on Ubuntu)
```bash
# put this folder in a workspace: ros2_ws/src/my_robot
cd ros2_ws
source /opt/ros/$ROS_DISTRO/setup.bash
colcon build --symlink-install
source install/setup.bash
ros2 launch my_robot robot_node.launch.py       # or: ros2 run my_robot robot_node
```
Inspect it: `ros2 topic list`, `ros2 topic echo /cmd_vel`, `ros2 topic hz /heartbeat`, `rqt_graph`.

Wire it to a real base with `ros2_control` (diff_drive_controller) or micro-ROS on an ESP32/STM32. For vision, add a node using the `robot-vision` template + `cv_bridge`.
